idiom_name: circe Encoder/Decoder/Codec typeclass instances (explicit or semi-derived)
implementation_notes: Translation is expressed as typeclass instances: Encoder[Order] and Decoder[Order] (or a combined Codec) written with Encoder.instance/Decoder.instance and cursor access (c.downField("order_id")), or derived from the case class with deriveDecoder/deriveEncoder and a configured member naming (circe.github.io). What replaces the classic structure is the implicit instance in the companion object, found by the compiler at the call site - there is no translator object to wire - and an explicit Translator class remains justified when the mapping is versioned per client, combines several formats, or needs injected collaborators.
pitfalls: Implicit resolution prefers the instance in the companion object of the static type, so a codec defined for a supertype can lose to the derived instance for the concrete class without a warning.
Automatic derivation (generic.auto) hides the mapping: failures arrive without the JSON path, making invalid messages hard to diagnose compared with explicit downField cursors.
circe-core contains no parser - io.circe.parser/jawn must be on the classpath (and the Scala.js build uses a different parser), otherwise asJson compiles but parsing is missing at runtime.
